overall_strategy:
Process each file line-by-line. First strip noise lines (see noise_strip_regexes) and detect/skip front matter: a leading table-of-contents block (SOMMAIRE / TABLE DES MATIERES / TABLE OF CONTENTS up to the first real structural marker) and gazette mastheads. Maintain a running "heading context" stack: whenever a line matches a part/book/title/chapter/section/subsection marker, update the corresponding slot in the stack (and clear all deeper slots). These heading lines are NOT chunks themselves; they only set context.

The chunk unit is the ARTICLE (or, for common-law-drafted English texts whose primary unit is the numbered SECTION — i.e. penal-en, and CM001EN whose articles are bare numbered clauses, treat the numbered clause/section as the article-equivalent). A chunk = the article marker line plus all following lines until the next marker of article-level OR any higher structural level (part/book/title/chapter/section), keeping numbered sub-paragraphs ((1), (2), 1), 2), a), bullet "!") together with their parent article. Preamble/Vu-clauses front matter that precedes the first article is emitted as its own chunk labeled articleSection="preamble".

Sizing/packing: (1) If an assembled article body <= max chars, emit as a single chunk. (2) If it exceeds max, window it: split on paragraph boundaries (blank line or sub-paragraph marker) into windows of <= max chars with `overlap` chars of trailing context repeated at the start of the next window; every window keeps the same article number/heading metadata plus a windowIndex/windowTotal. (3) If an article body < min chars, greedily pack it with subsequent consecutive small articles (same enclosing heading context only) until reaching min..max; record the spanned article range (e.g. "12-14") in articleSection. Never merge across a higher-level boundary. Normalize internal whitespace (collapse multi-space OCR gaps, join hyphenated line-wraps like "tra-\nvail" -> "travail") before measuring/emitting.
bilingual_handling: Corpus is overwhelmingly single-language per file; set chunk.language from the file's detected dominant language (fr or en). Two bilingual situations: (a) Header/title front matter that prints both REPUBLIC OF CAMEROON / REPUBLIQUE DU CAMEROUN and English statute titles (regime-foncier-fr) — the body is mono-language, so strip the foreign-language masthead lines via noise regexes and tag the whole file fr; do NOT create EN chunks from quoted legal terms ('freehold lands' etc.) embedded in French articles. (b) If a file genuinely interleaves EN and FR translation blocks per article (sequential-blocks layout), detect the language of each assembled chunk by majority script/stopword heuristic and set chunk.language accordingly, emitting the FR and EN versions as separate chunks that share the same articleNumber and citation but differ in language and a langVariant flag. For regime-foncier specifically there are NO interleaved translation blocks, so treat it as fr-only.
metadata_rules: Per chunk emit: articleNumber (from article_number_capture; "PREMIER" normalized to "1"; preserve compound "133-1" and Latin suffix e.g. "12 bis"; null for preamble/Vu chunks). articleSection = canonical label of the chunk: for a single article "Article 12" (or "Section 12" for penal-en / CM001EN bare-numbered), for a packed range "Articles 12-14", for a windowed long article "Article 12 (part 2/3)", for front matter "preamble". headingPath = ordered breadcrumb from the enclosing-context stack joined by " > ", e.g. "PARTIE 2 > LIVRE 1 > TITRE 1 > Chapitre 1 > Section 1"; include only the levels actually present above the chunk (omit empty slots). citation = human-readable reference built from doc-level title + article, e.g. "Constitution 1996 (Loi n°96/06), art. 1"; "Code pénal 2016, art. 25-1"; "AUSCGIE (OHADA), art. 133-1"; "Code du travail 1992 (Loi n°92-007), art. 12"; "CGI 2024, art. 2 bis"; "Ordonnance n°81/002 du 29 juin 1981, art. 5"; "Ordonnance n°74-1 du 6 juillet 1974, art. 3"; "Copyright Law No. 2000/011, s. 3". Also store docId, docType, language, and (for regime-foncier) which of the two sequential ordinances the chunk belongs to. Preserve any in-article amendment markers ("(nouveau)", "(Ordonnance 77-1...)") inside the chunk text and copy them into an amendments metadata field.
per_type_notes: constitution (const-fr): PREAMBULE is its own chunk; 'ARTICLE PREMIER :' -> articleNumber 1; sub-sections (1)(2)(3) stay with the article; '(nouveau)' tags amendments — keep and record.

code FR (penal-fr, labour-fr, cgi-fr): hierarchy LIVRE>TITRE>CHAPITRE>SECTION(>SOUS-SECTION)>Article; markers 'ARTICLE 1.-' and 'Art.1.-' and 'Article 2.-' all map to the article level; CGI adds Latin suffixes (bis/ter/...) and SOUS-SECTION level — capture suffix in articleNumber.

code EN (penal-en): common-law PART>BOOK>CHAPTER>SECTION; primary unit is SECTION ('SECTION 25-1:'); treat SECTION as the article-equivalent for chunking and put the number in articleNumber; tolerate OCR like 'Ill'->III and spacing 'Exec ution'.

uniform-act (auscgie-fr): full PARTIE>LIVRE>TITRE>CHAPITRE>Section>Article chain with mixed case (Chapitre/Section lowercase-initial); compound article numbers 2-1 etc; up to ~920 articles; strip long TOC and repeated JO footers.
ordinance (etat-civil-fr): 'Article N. —' em-dash; preamble Vu-clauses kept as a preamble chunk; signature block (Yaoundé... AHMADOU AHIDJO) stripped as boilerplate.

ordinance (regime-foncier-fr): ONE file = TWO ordinances (74-1 then 74-2) with article numbering that RESETS; detect the second 'Ordonnance n°...' header and start a new doc-scope so duplicate article numbers don't collide; markers may be OCR-mangled ('Orc}onnance','ART.'); the bare-capitalized-phrase section regex is unreliable — prefer TITRE/CHAPITRE/ARTICLE markers only.

statute EN (CM001EN): articles are bare 'N.—(1)' / 'N.—' with NO 'Article' word; use the digit+period+em-dash article regex; ensure it fires only at line start to avoid catching sub-clause numbers; PART/Chapter in title-case.
edge_cases: regime-foncier-fr packs two ordinances in one file with article numbers reset — split on the second ordinance header into two doc scopes; never pack/window across that boundary; record the source ordinance in metadata so 'art. 2' is disambiguated.

Low/degraded text-layer OCR (penal-fr, penal-en, regime-foncier): article markers survive but headers/footers are garbled; rely on fuzzy noise regexes (PRESIDENCE..., COPIE CERTI..., SECRETARIA...) and join hyphenated wraps; if an article body is mostly garbage but the marker is valid, still emit the chunk (retrieval-better-than-nothing) and set a lowQuality flag.

Huge tax code (cgi-fr-2024, 614+ articles) with tables/annexes: tables (rows of numbers/pipes/tabs) can exceed max — when windowing a table-heavy article, prefer to split on row boundaries and never break mid-row; keep the article header line repeated at the top of each window; annexes after the last LIVRE keep their own headingPath.

Gazette/JO mastheads and signature/certification blocks (auscgie footers, etat-civil signature, presidential letterheads) are recurring boilerplate — strip via noise regexes; a chunk must never be ONLY masthead/signature text.

Front-matter TOC with dot-leaders ('Article 5 ....... 12') must not be mistaken for article starts — only treat a marker as an article boundary AFTER the TOC region (i.e. after the first non-TOC structural marker / once dot-leader+page-number pattern stops).
'ARTICLE PREMIER' / 'TITRE PREMIER' / 'PARTIE PREMIERE' — normalize PREMIER(E) to 1 in numbers.
Compound and amended numbers (25-1, 133-1, '12 bis (nouveau)') must round-trip into articleNumber without losing the suffix or amendment tag.

Bare-number English clauses (CM001EN) could collide with sub-paragraph numbering; the line-start em-dash anchor and post-TOC gating prevent false splits; verify the next line is article-like prose, not a continuation.

Very short trailing articles (e.g. 'Article 22.- La présente loi sera publiée...') get packed with neighbors but a final lone tiny article with no same-context neighbor is emitted alone rather than merged across a TITRE boundary.
